name: Unihealth Hospitals Ltd
tagline: High-growth Africa hospital platform (Uganda crown jewel) now expanding into India — real operating momentum, but P/E ~50, SME liquidity and a minority-owned India vehicle cap conviction
business_overview: Unihealth Hospitals (formerly Unihealth Medical Consultancy; NSE SME: UNIHEALTH) operates hospitals and medical centres primarily in Uganda (its mature, cash-generative core), plus consultancy services, pharma exports/distribution, and now an India expansion (Navi Mumbai and Nashik hospitals) run through UMC Hospitals Pvt Ltd. Exited Nigeria in FY25. Active ValuePickr thread (55 posts) read to July 2026.
fundamentals_table: FY26 revenue ~Rs 1.32bn, +33% YoY; multi-year ~135% headline growth, ~38.6% 5-yr PAT CAGR
P/E ~50, P/B high; debtor days ~341 (structural, African govt payment cycles)
fundamentals_narrative: Growth and returns are genuinely strong (ROCE ~24.5%, FY26 revenue +33%, Uganda growing ~25% and now debt-free) and management guides to 350-400 operational beds by FY26 and ~1,000 beds within two years. Against that: the stock has already run roughly 6x in a year to a ~50x P/E; ~341 debtor days is a real working-capital drag; the India growth vehicle (UMC Hospitals Pvt Ltd) is only ~80-82% owned by the listed company with the remainder held by non-promoters including promoters personally; and a July 2026 share-swap took Victoria Hospital (Uganda) to ~99.81% owned, adding ~Rs 25.5 Cr EBITDA / ~Rs 21.75 Cr PAT.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. 52-week range Rs 134-820; the stock has re-rated ~6x and had an 85%-in-7-sessions burst per news, i.e. extremely extended.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 55 posts (first-time read), spanning Jan 2025 to July 2026. Sentiment is constructive but genuinely two-sided: strong H1 FY26 results ('classic operating leverage'), detailed bull models toward 1,000 beds, Uganda debt-free and tax-free — versus a stretched valuation, ~341 debtor days, and a governance debate over the 80%-owned India subsidiary. One participant (drkshetty1, non-trusted) disclosed exiting into the rally, citing valuation and 'too many businesses.'
community_signal: Three 'elevated'-tier roster users are active and constructive (no conviction floor applies): pranavpallod12 (multiple posts, 4-6 loves) frames the company at an inflection — Uganda moat funding India optionality, thesis 'could be very big or flat' — and says H1 FY26 'surpassed all expectations'; Satishwe (8 loves) built a detailed guidance-based model; niraj (5 loves) logged the July 2026 Victoria Hospital consolidation. Counterweights from non-trusted users: Mayank_Jham's math implies only ~35% EBITDA growth to FY28E (valuation stretched) and Agni's flag that the minority-owned India vehicle is a structural governance concern. No formal high-conviction BUY call from a very-high-tier user.
bse_notes: July 2026 share-swap raised Unihealth's stake in Victoria Hospital (Uganda) to ~99.81% (from ~50%), accretive by ~Rs 25.5 Cr EBITDA / ~Rs 21.75 Cr PAT. India expansion via UMC Hospitals Pvt Ltd, ~80-82% owned by the listed entity. Not independently re-verified beyond forum-linked disclosures.
bull_case: Genuine high growth (FY26 revenue +33%) with strong returns (ROCE ~24.5%) and a mature, now debt-free, tax-advantaged Uganda core
Specific, named expansion pipeline: 350-400 beds by FY26, ~1,000 beds within two years, plus Tanzania
Victoria Hospital consolidation (July 2026) is immediately EBITDA/PAT accretive
Three 'elevated'-tier roster users actively engaged and constructive on the operating trajectory
bear_case: Stock already ~6x in a year to a ~50x P/E — a lot of good news is priced in, and one community model implies only ~35% EBITDA growth to FY28E
NSE-SME listing: structurally thin liquidity for the market cap
~341 debtor days is a real working-capital drag even if partly structural to African government payment cycles
India growth vehicle only ~80-82% owned by the listed company, with promoters holding a personal minority stake — a governance structure the community itself flags as a red flag
Single-country revenue concentration (Uganda) and hard-to-verify African operations
verdict_headline: Real operating momentum and a credible bed-expansion pipeline keep a 10x case alive, but valuation, SME liquidity and the India-vehicle structure hold conviction to Low
verdict_reasoning: FY26 revenue +33%, ROCE ~24.5%, a debt-free Uganda core funding India optionality, and an accretive Victoria consolidation support a 10x-in-2-3-years framing on execution of the 1,000-bed plan

Conviction is Low: a ~50x P/E after a ~6x run, NSE-SME liquidity, ~341 debtor days, and a minority-owned India subsidiary are unresolved risks — and the roster support, while genuine, is 'elevated' tier with no formal BUY call
Old 108-stock project rated this Tier B; re-derived under the open-screen thesis it stays a 10x candidate but explicitly valuation-gated and unconfirmed

trusted_signals.signal: Constructive: H1 FY26 'surpassed all expectations'; Uganda moat (25% growth, tax-free, debt-free) cushions India commissioning costs; big upside if the 1,000-bed plan executes. Not a formal position call.
Logged the July 2026 share-swap taking Victoria Hospital (Uganda) to ~99.81% owned, accretive ~Rs 25.5 Cr EBITDA / ~Rs 21.75 Cr PAT — informational, constructive.

four_box.note: 1,000-bed expansion plan on debt-free Uganda-funded base is real, sizeable headroom (tailwind/tam=yes); ~50x P/E after a ~6x run (valuation=no).
